column1: # LUTHERSTRASSE 34 IS STANDESAMT CHARLOTTENBURG I — AND THE CHAIN IS FOUR PAGES, EVERY ONE READ AT THE IMAGE.
# Berliner Adressbuch 1913, Zentral- und Landesbibliothek Berlin, record 34115495_1913. Read 8 October 2026.
# WHY IT WAS STUCK. Work list row 241 has been blocked since 22 September on "which of the Charlottenburg
# registry offices served Lutherstrasse 34", and it was looking for the answer in a STREET DIRECTORY.
# IT IS NOT IN ONE, AND IT NEVER WAS. The Berlin Teil III heading for a street belonging to an independent
# suburb gives the COURT and not the registry office, and Charlottenburg's own offices are defined by
# STADTBEZIRK rather than by street. The question needed a different page, not a better search.
field
*** JACOB LEIBHOLZ'S 1913 REGISTRY OFFICE IS STANDESAMT CHARLOTTENBURG I, RANKESTRASSE 10 ***
column2: Standesbeamter in 1913: v. FISCHER-TREUENFELD. Printed page 505 of the Charlottenburg part: "Standesamt I. Rankestr. 10. UMFASSEND DIE STADTBEZIRKE HOCHSCHULVIERTEL 1-7, AM KURFÜRSTENDAMM 1-6, OSTVIERTEL 1-8." Read at the image; the crop is site/public/charlottenburg-standesamt-i-1913.png.

column1: and the link that joins the street to the office
column2: printed page 673, the Charlottenburg "Stadtteile und Stadtbezirke" list: *** OSTVIERTEL 2 = Augsburger Str. 1-13 and 61-74 · Bayreuther Str. 22-36 · Eisenacher Str. 1-8 · Geisbergstr. 1-9 · Kalckreuthstr. · Kleiststr. 23-35 · LUTHERSTR. 12-43 · Motzstr. 13-21 · Wormser Straße. *** 34 falls inside 12-43. Read at the image; crop in site/public/ostviertel-2-1913.png.

column1: *** AND THE HOUSE ITSELF CROSS-CHECKS IT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT ONE READING BUT TWO ***
column2: the street section entry opens "34 S. A. AUGSBURGER STR. 4" — NUMBER 34 IS A CORNER BUILDING and carries a second address on Augsburger Straße. AUGSBURGER STR. 1-13 IS ALSO OSTVIERTEL 2. Both faces of the same building land in the same Stadtbezirk and therefore the same office. A single street range could be a misread; two independent addresses agreeing is not.

column1: # ---------------- THE HOUSE, WHICH NOBODY HAD EVER OPENED ----------------
*** THE OCR SAYS THE LEIBHOLZ ENTRY IS AT NUMBER 31. THE IMAGE SAYS 34. ***
column2: Teil III, printed page 535, column 1. The ALTO word layer reads "31" and the Fraktur numeral on the page is unmistakably **34** — the open-topped Fraktur 4 is read as a 1. HAD THIS BEEN TAKEN FROM THE TEXT LAYER IT WOULD HAVE CONTRADICTED TEIL I AND PUT THE WHOLE IDENTIFICATION IN DOUBT. It agrees with Teil I exactly: "LEIBHOLZ, JAQUES, Kaufm., W 62, Lutherstr. 34 II."

column1: LUTHERSTRASSE 34 IN 1913, THE WHOLE HOUSEHOLD

column1: what the household is and is not evidence of
column2: A LARGE MIXED-TRADE APARTMENT HOUSE with a delicatessen, a photographic studio, a boarding house and a bookseller in it, owned by a lawyer and run by a manager. Several of the names are ones a reader will want to read something into — Aron, Aufrichtig, Mendel, Schlesinger. THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT. A surname is not a religion and a shared address is not a relationship; the names are recorded because they are on the page and because an address with sixteen households is the opposite of a private one.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THIS OPENS, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE ROW ----------------
THE READABLE QUESTION IS NOW A SMALL ONE
column2: Standesamt Charlottenburg I holds, in the Landesarchiv's free online set, 15 BIRTH index volumes (1898-1901 to 1914), 10 MARRIAGE (1898-1900 to 1935-1938) and 10 DEATH (1898-1901 to 1938) — 35 volumes, not the 114 of all three offices. JACOB WAS AT LUTHERSTRASSE 34 IN 1913, ELEVEN YEARS BEFORE HE MARRIED AUGUSTE, and this archive has never held a document about him from before 1924 except a directory line.

column1: and the closure periods bound what can be found
column2: births stop at 1914 and marriages and deaths run to 1938, so a FIRST MARRIAGE, a death in his household, or an acknowledgement of paternity in Charlottenburg between 1898 and 1938 is reachable and free. A birth after 1914 is not online at any price.

column1: # ---------------- TWO THINGS CORRECTED, AND ONE LEFT OPEN ----------------
THE "TWO LUTHERSTRASSEN" TRAP IS NOW NAVIGABLE RATHER THAN JUST FLAGGED
column2: row 241 warned that promising hits were registrars' own home addresses in "W 62, Lutherstr." THE DISTRICT LIST SETTLES WHERE W 62's LUTHERSTRASSE RAN: between Kleiststraße, Motzstraße, Wormser Straße, Augsburger Straße, Nettelbeckstraße and Courbièrestraße, crossing Kurfürstenstraße — the Wittenbergplatz to Nollendorfplatz blocks. The street is bounded by its neighbours now, not by its name.

column1: and the Berlin street heading was read correctly and simply does not carry the answer
column2: printed page 534: "W. 62 LUTHERSTR. · A.G. CHARLOTTB. — L.G. III. · (GEH. Z. CHARLOTTENBURG)". The same page shows the pattern on another street — "W. 50 Präger Str. (geh. z. Wilmersdorf.) A.G. Charlottb. — L.G. III." *** THE BERLIN DIRECTORY GIVES THE COURT FOR A SUBURB STREET AND NOT THE STANDESAMT, because the suburb ran its own offices. *** Row 241 spent two sessions looking for a column that was never there.

column1: STILL OPEN AND NOT GUESSED AT
column2: what W 62's Lutherstraße is called today. Its neighbours are all still on the map, so the stretch is locatable, but no source read here names the successor street and this archive has already been wrong once in this file by reasoning from a name. Kauperts should be re-read for the NORTHERN section of Martin-Luther-Straße specifically, which is a different question from the one asked on 20 September.
